content:
For years, collectors have clamored for Jobs memorabilia, and a new piece seems poised to generate significant interest: his eighth-grade science fair project, complete with two demonstration circuits and a warning note he wrote to his teacher.

The project has been kept at the Jobs family property in Los Altos, but is now one of more than 200 lots in an Apple 50th anniversary auction...

Celebrating 50 years this year, Apple has been honored by RR Auction with a two-part sale dubbed "Steve Jobs & the Computer Revolution: The Apple 50th Anniversary Auction." The first part saw the company's first check written sell for up to $2.4 million.

The second part includes the science fair project.

The warning note appears to warn that the circuits might burn out if left on too long. Online bids were below $3,000 at the time of writing, but that is sure to change.

There's also a fully functional early Apple 1 computer.

And a development prototype of the original iPod.
